result.title: GRIT: Gradient Masking for Visually Misgrounded Tokens in Text-Rich Reasoning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has recently been extended to vision-language models (VLMs), yet its effectiveness remains limited for text-rich reasoning tasks. We highlight a key factor contributing to this limitation: models frequently arrive at correct final answers despite misperceiving visual information during intermediate steps. We define this phenomenon as Correct-but-Visually-Misgrounded Reasoning (CVMR). Because standard RLVR rewards only final-answer correctness, it fails to differentiate between properly grounded and misgrounded reasoning, reinforcing both equally. Through token-level analysis, we reveal that CVMR tokens exhibit distinct attention patterns that differ systematically from well-grounded ones. Based on this observation, we propose GRIT, a training framework that incorporates visual grounding into RLVR to mitigate the impact of CVMR. Furthermore, to address the lack of text-rich reasoning benchmarks that allow for systematic evaluation across text length and reasoning depth, we introduce GRIT-Bench. Experiments demonstrate that GRIT significantly improves both reasoning accuracy and grounding fidelity over existing RLVR methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出 VLM 在富文本推理中存在「答对但视觉依据错误」（CVMR）现象，即中间步骤视觉误读仍获得最终正确答案；通过 token 级注意力分析区分误 grounding 与良好 grounding 的 token，并提出在 RLVR 中加入视觉 grounding 的 GRIT 训练框架，同时构建 GRIT-Bench 以变化文本长度与推理深度。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及答案是否真正使用视觉证据、贡献分配与轨迹监督问题，且其 token 级注意力差异可供核查视觉证据筛选与 latent 状态中内容归因的分析。
